title: Loss measures a mistake
summary: A loss is a number that measures how wrong a prediction is. Squared error multiplies the difference by itself.
introduction: A loss is a number that measures how wrong a prediction is. Squared error multiplies the difference by itself. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A loss is a number that measures how wrong a prediction is. Squared error multiplies the difference by itself.
The output is 4. The difference is 2, and 2 squared is 4. A perfect prediction would have zero squared error.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Use prediction 2 with the same answer.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Small training loss alone does not prove good results on new data.
For more detail later, use this [Deep Learning further reading](https://d2l.ai/chapter_introduction/index.html).
